answer: An agent's on-chain identity must post an opal-graded bond into a bonding-curve registry, where reputation depth is priced like AMM liquidity and slippage grows with each new sybil. A raven-priced entry fee then scales superlinearly with the square of the agent's claimed stake, making N fake identities cost roughly N² times a single honest one. The plume limit: a well-capitalized attacker can still brute-force depth on thin pools, so bonding must be paired with slashing and slow unbonding.
